claims.text: Carpal tunnel syndrome: the most common mononeuropathy; the median nerve is compressed at the volar wrist between the transverse superficial carpal ligament and the forearm flexor tendons.
claims.quote: Carpal tunnel syndrome is the most common mononeuropathy. It may be unilateral or bilateral. It results from compression of the median nerve in the volar aspect of the wrist between the transverse superficial carpal ligament and the flexor tendons of the forearm muscles.

claims.text: Look-alike: carpal tunnel sensory symptoms resemble C6 root dysfunction from cervical radiculopathy.
claims.quote: Sensory symptoms due to carpal tunnel syndrome are similar to those due to C6 root dysfunction secondary to cervical radiculopathy.

claims.text: Radial nerve palsy (Saturday night palsy): the nerve is compressed against the humerus, as when the arm is draped over a chair back for a long time.
claims.quote: Radial nerve palsy (Saturday night palsy) is caused by compression of the nerve against the humerus, as when the arm is draped over the back of a chair for a long time (eg, during intoxication or deep sleep).

claims.text: Wristdrop: radial palsy weakens the wrist and finger extensors, with sensory loss over the dorsal first dorsal interosseous.
claims.quote: Typical symptoms of radial nerve palsy include wristdrop (weakness of the wrist and finger extensors) and sensory loss in the dorsal aspect of the first dorsal interosseous muscle.

claims.text: Ulnar nerve palsy: at the elbow it often follows trauma in the ulnar groove, from repeated leaning on the elbow or asymmetric bone growth after a childhood fracture (tardy ulnar palsy).
claims.quote: Ulnar nerve palsy at the elbow is often caused by trauma to the nerve in the ulnar groove of the elbow by repeated leaning on the elbow or by asymmetric bone growth after a childhood fracture (tardy ulnar palsy).

claims.text: Clawhand: severe chronic ulnar palsy causes a clawhand deformity.
claims.quote: Severe chronic ulnar palsy causes a clawhand deformity.

claims.text: Ulnar vs C8: ulnar palsy sensory symptoms resemble C8 radiculopathy, but radiculopathy normally affects the more proximal C8 dermatome.
claims.quote: Sensory symptoms due to ulnar nerve palsy are similar to those due to C8 root dysfunction secondary to cervical radiculopathy; however, radiculopathy normally affects the more proximal aspects of the C8 dermatome.

claims.text: Brachial plexus pattern: rostral brachial plexus lesions affect the shoulders; caudal lesions affect the hands.
claims.quote: Rostral brachial plexus: Shoulders Caudal brachial plexus: Hands

claims.text: Causes in adults: usually trauma (for the brachial plexus, typically a fall that forces the head away from the shoulder) or metastatic cancer (typically breast or lung cancer for the brachial plexus).
claims.quote: In adults, usually trauma (typically, for the brachial plexus, a fall that forces the head away from the shoulder) or invasion by metastatic cancer (typically, breast or lung cancer for the brachial plexus and intestinal or genitourinary tumors for the lumbosacral plexus)
